result:
UI consistency audit complete. All 7 charter audits run across 16 routes; **1 defect found and fixed**.

## The defect — `/calendar` priority badge could never show a colour

`CalendarView.jsx:140` renders `` calendar-event-content__priority--${priority} ``. That `priority` comes from `tasks.priority`, whose column type is the `lead_priority` enum — **exactly `hot | warm | cold`** (verified against the live DB, not just the migration). But `index.css` defined modifiers for `--urgent/--high/--medium/--low`.

The set difference was total: **0 of 3 reachable values had a rule, 0 of 4 defined rules could ever match.** The base class supplies padding/radius but no background and no color, so the badge rendered transparent on every calendar event — a colour-coded indicator structurally incapable of showing a colour.

Fixed in CSS only, renaming the modifiers to the real enum values on the same red/amber/blue hues the app already uses at `.lead-table__priority-dot--hot/warm/cold`. Verified twice: a DOM-injection probe measured `rgba(0,0,0,0)` for all three values beforehand, and afterward a **real rendered calendar event** measured `oklch(0.55 0.17 85 / 0.3)`. Also confirmed in the built CSS, not just `src`.

**Why 5 prior UI audits missed it** — two reusable reasons: it never renders today (all 4 tasks have `due_date NULL`), so it's invisible to any screenshot or computed-style sweep; and an *interpolated* modifier is invisible to the static className-vs-CSS diff earlier runs used, since neither side ever contains the runtime name.

The finding came from a new set difference — interpolated modifier classes vs the enum values that can flow in, resolved down to the DB column type. The app has **exactly four** such families and all four are now resolved, so that check is closed rather than sampled.

## Everything else passed

Headers 56px on all 16 routes with zero variance; sidebar 18 links / 18 icons (all `0 0 24 24`) / 42px / exactly 1 active; **0 native `<select>` and 0 native date inputs** (9th consecutive run); 13 `.modal-backdrop` + 5 `.slide-over` with 0 overlays using neither; 0 foreign icons anywhere. The button-radius spread reduced entirely to already-documented `clamp()` artifacts and deliberate segmented controls — I changed nothing there.

## One thing I did not fix, deliberately

`automationEngine.js:75-77` inserts `cfg.priority || 'medium'` into that same `lead_priority` enum column. Every value `AutomationSettings.jsx` offers, plus the default, is an invalid enum label — so any automation rule that creates a task should fail with `22P02`. That's a server defect and outside the UI-audit charter, so I documented it for the next api-test stage rather than touching it. It's also the origin of the CSS mismatch above.

Two commits: `7d90e86` (fix) and `a75ce63` (report). Build passes, working tree clean, no stray screenshots, and **net zero DB rows** — the one `due_date` I set to make the badge observable was reverted (0 → 1 → 0, total 4 throughout). Memory and the resume log are updated for the next run.
